claim: Layer 5 pyramidal neurons (L5PNs) are thought to be central to cortical computation because of their extensive arborisation and nonlinear dendritic operations.
source: Layer 5 pyramidal neurons (L5PNs) in particular are thought to be central to cortical computation because of their extensive arborisation and nonlinear dendritic operations.
evidence: This is a statement about the general understanding in the field, supported by established scientific knowledge about L5PNs.

claim: L5PNs in the secondary visual cortex show reduced dendritic excitability compared to primary visual cortex.
source: L5PNs in the secondary visual cortex show reduced dendritic excitability and smaller propensity for burst firing.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: L5PNs in the secondary visual cortex show smaller propensity for burst firing compared to primary visual cortex.
source: L5PNs in the secondary visual cortex show reduced dendritic excitability and smaller propensity for burst firing.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The reduced excitability in V2m L5PNs is correlated with shorter apical dendrites.
source: This reduced excitability is correlated with shorter apical dendrites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data showing correlation between apical trunk length and excitability.

claim: Apical length influences dendritic backpropagation and excitability through a Na+ channel-dependent broadening of backpropagating action potentials.
source: Using numerical modelling, we uncover a universal principle underlying the influence of apical length on dendritic backpropagation and excitability, based on a Na+ channel-dependent broadening of backpropagating action potentials.
evidence: This is a primary finding from computational modeling experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The operational repertoire of L5PNs is not universal throughout the brain.
source: In summary, we provide new insights into the modulation of dendritic excitability by apical dendrite length and show that the operational repertoire of L5PNs is not universal throughout the brain.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data showing differences between V1 and V2m.

claim: The neocortex is thought to have a modular structure composed of 'canonical circuits' performing stereotyped computations.
source: The neocortex is thought to have a modular structure composed of 'canonical circuits' performing stereotyped computations (Harris and Shepherd, 2015; Markram et al., 2015; Miller, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Anatomical evidence supports the existence of repeating circuit architectures that display similar general features across species and brain areas.
source: Anatomical evidence supports the existence of repeating circuit architectures that display similar general features across species and brain areas (Carlo and Stevens, 2013; Douglas and Martin, 2004; Mountcastle, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Architectural motifs in the neocortex are thought to serve as a physical substrate to perform a small range of specific, canonical computations.
source: It is generally thought that these architectural motifs serve as a physical substrate to perform a small range of specific, canonical computations (Bastos et al., 2012; Braganza and Beck, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pyramidal neurons have biophysical attributes that endow them with nonlinear properties allowing them to implement a repertoire of advanced computations at the single cell level.
source: Across brain areas and species, their biophysical attributes endow them with nonlinear properties that allow them to implement a repertoire of advanced computations at the single cell level (Gidon et al., 2020; London and Häusser, 2005; Spruston, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: L5PN dendritic nonlinearities enable signal amplification and coincidence detection of inputs.
source: Their dendritic nonlinearities enable signal amplification and coincidence detection of inputs – a crucial operation to integrate feedforward and feedback streams that often send projections onto separate dendritic domains.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about L5PN function.

claim: A single backpropagating action potential (bAP), when combined with distal synaptic input, can trigger a burst of somatic action potentials in L5PNs.
source: In these cells, a single backpropagating action potential (bAP), when combined with distal synaptic input, can trigger a burst of somatic action potentials.
evidence: This statement is based on established knowledge about L5PN function.

claim: The all-or-none dendritic Ca2+ plateau is the crucial mechanism underlying the nonlinear burst phenomenon in L5PNs.
source: The crucial mechanism underlying this nonlinear phenomenon is the all-or-none dendritic Ca2+ plateau (Larkum et al., 1999a; Larkum et al., 1999b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Morphology and intrinsic properties have a profound influence on neuronal excitability.
source: Morphology and intrinsic properties have a profound influence on neuronal excitability.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established neuroscience knowledge.

claim: Dendritic topology and the electrical coupling between the soma and dendrites are thought to be particularly crucial for determining a neuron's integrative properties.
source: Dendritic topology and the electrical coupling between the soma and dendrites are thought to be particularly crucial for determining a neuron's integrative properties (Mainen and Sejnowski, 1996; Schaefer et al., 2003; van Ooyen et al., 2002; Vetter et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: There can be substantial variation in intrinsic properties of L5PNs depending on the location within a cortical area or on the species they are recorded from.
source: Recent experimental work has shown that there can be substantial variation in intrinsic properties of L5PNs depending on the location within a cortical area or on the species they are recorded from (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2018; Fletcher and Williams, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: It is often assumed that pyramidal neurons have robust enough properties across cortical areas and brain structures to support similar computations.
source: However, it is often assumed that pyramidal neurons have robust enough properties across cortical areas and brain structures to support similar computations (Bastos et al., 2012; Hawkins et al., 2017; Larkum, 2013; Shipp, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Hippocampal pyramidal neurons display dendritic Ca2+ APs that support coincidence detection of distal and proximal inputs, analogous to L5PNs.
source: For instance, analogous to L5PNs, hippocampal pyramidal neurons also display dendritic Ca2+ APs that support coincidence detection of distal and proximal inputs (Jarsky et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Whole-cell patch clamp recordings were made from ttL5 neurons in V1 and V2m in acutely prepared mouse brain slices.
source: We made whole-cell patch clamp recordings from ttL5 neurons in V1 and V2m in acutely prepared mouse brain slices.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Recordings were restricted to L5PNs projecting to the lateral posterior nucleus of thalamus (n = 117), identified using retrograde labelling with cholera toxin subunit B (CTB).
source: To ensure consistency in cell type, recordings were restricted to L5PNs projecting to the lateral posterior nucleus of thalamus (n = 117), identified using retrograde labelling with cholera toxin subunit B (CTB, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–E), or to neurons labelled in the Colgalt2-Cre mouse line (n = 12) known to be ttL5 PNs (Groh et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology and cell identification used in the study.

claim: Recordings were made from neurons labelled in the Colgalt2-Cre mouse line (n = 12) known to be ttL5 PNs.
source: To ensure consistency in cell type, recordings were restricted to L5PNs projecting to the lateral posterior nucleus of thalamus (n = 117), identified using retrograde labelling with cholera toxin subunit B (CTB, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–E), or to neurons labelled in the Colgalt2-Cre mouse line (n = 12) known to be ttL5 PNs (Groh et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology and cell identification used in the study, with citation support for the Colgalt2-Cre line labeling ttL5 PNs.

claim: BAC firing was observed in approximately half the recorded V1 neurons (10/21).
source: In summary, BAC firing was observed in approximately half the recorded V1 neurons (10/21), while neurons in V2m showed an almost total lack of BAC firing (1/18, p = 4.6*10−3, Fisher's exact test, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Neurons in V2m showed an almost total lack of BAC firing (1/18).
source: In summary, BAC firing was observed in approximately half the recorded V1 neurons (10/21), while neurons in V2m showed an almost total lack of BAC firing (1/18, p = 4.6*10−3, Fisher's exact test, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The difference in BAC firing between V1 and V2m is statistically significant (p = 4.6*10−3, Fisher's exact test).
source: In summary, BAC firing was observed in approximately half the recorded V1 neurons (10/21), while neurons in V2m showed an almost total lack of BAC firing (1/18, p = 4.6*10−3, Fisher's exact test, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: CGP52432 (1 µM) was added to the extracellular solution to avoid recruiting inhibitory inputs during extracellular stimulation.
source: To avoid recruiting inhibitory inputs during the extracellular stimulation and create the most favourable conditions to enable BAC firing (Pérez-Garci et al., 2006), we added the competitive GABAB receptor antagonist CGP52432 (1 µM) to the extracellular solution.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology with citation support for the rationale.

claim: For neurons with a defined critical frequency, the mean values in V1 (112 ± 31 Hz, n = 26) and in V2m neurons (109 ± 26 Hz, n = 11) did not differ significantly (p = 0.82; two-sample t-test).
source: For neurons with a defined critical frequency, the mean values in V1 (112 ± 31 Hz, n = 26) and in V2m neurons (109 ± 26 Hz, n = 11) did not differ significantly (p = 0.82; two-sample t-test; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: Neurons in V2m had significantly smaller ADP area compared to V1 (V1 mean = 91 ± 50 mV*ms, SD, n = 41; V2m mean = 42 ± 33 mV*ms, SD, n = 49; p = 4.54 * 10−6, D = 0.52; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
source: Neurons in V2m had significantly smaller ADP area (V1 mean = 91 ± 50 mV*ms, SD, n = 41; V2m mean = 42 ± 33 mV*ms, SD, n = 49; p = 4.54 * 10−6, D = 0.52; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), reflecting that most of these cells lacked a critical frequency altogether.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with statistical analysis.

claim: Most V2m cells lacked a critical frequency altogether.
source: Neurons in V2m had significantly smaller ADP area (V1 mean = 91 ± 50 mV*ms, SD, n = 41; V2m mean = 42 ± 33 mV*ms, SD, n = 49; p = 4.54 * 10−6, D = 0.52; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), reflecting that most of these cells lacked a critical frequency altogether.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on ADP area.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in maximum ADP integral values between 1.5 mM and 2 mM CaCl2 conditions in either V1 or V2m.
source: Although some change in the magnitude of Ca2+ currents is expected, at the level of maximum ADP integral values there was no statistically significant difference between the two conditions in either V1 or V2m (p = 0.12, D = 0.36 for V1; p = 0.21, D = 0.29 for V2m; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no significant difference in the maximum ADP integral values across V2m neurons labelled retrogradely or by the Colgalt2-Cre line (p = 0.62, D = 0.24; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
source: Similarly, as there was no significant difference in the maximum ADP integral values across V2m neurons labelled retrogradely or by the Colgalt2-Cre line (p = 0.62, D = 0.24; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Figure 2—figure supplement 2), we pooled these populations.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The percentage of neurons with cfADP was more than three times higher in V1 than in V2m (p = 2.6*10−5, Fisher's exact test).
source: The percentage of neurons with cfADP, as determined by the classification, was more than three times higher in V1 than in V2m (p = 2.6*10−5, Fisher's exact test, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Apical trunk lengths were significantly shorter in V2m than in V1 (V1 mean = 409 ± 64 µm, SD, n = 22 vs V2m mean = 313 ± 65 µm, SD, n = 26; p = 4.26*10−6, two-sample t-test).
source: Apical trunk lengths were significantly shorter in V2m than in V1 (V1 mean = 409 ± 64 µm, SD, n = 22 vs V2m mean = 313 ± 65 µm, SD, n = 26; p = 4.26*10−6, two-sample t-test, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 2C.

claim: There was a correlation between maximum ADP integral values and apical trunk length across the two populations (p = 5.37*10−3; F-test).
source: Additionally, there was a correlation between maximum ADP integral values and apical trunk length across the two populations (p = 5.37*10−3; F-test).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Dendritic length and number of branchpoints for the tuft and basal dendrites as well as the number of oblique branches were similar between V1 and V2m populations.
source: Dendritic length and number of branchpoints for the tuft and basal dendrites as well as the number of oblique branches were similar between the two populations.
evidence: This is a finding from morphological analysis of reconstructed neurons.

claim: Apical length, convex hull and largest Sholl radius were significantly greater in the V1 neurons (p < 0.005 Bonferroni-corrected two sample t-test).
source: Apical length, convex hull and largest Sholl radius, however, were significantly greater in the V1 neurons (p < 0.005 Bonferroni-corrected two sample t-test, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B,C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with statistical analysis and reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 4B,C.

claim: Coincident stimulation triggered BAC firing in the detailed model with long morphology.
source: Mirroring the responses seen in the subset of strongly bursting ttL5 neurons, coincident stimulation triggered BAC firing in the detailed model (Figure 3A, left).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: With short morphology from V2m, coincident tuft and somatic stimulation evoked only a single somatic spike and did not trigger a dendritic Ca2+ plateau.
source: With this short morphology from V2m, coincident tuft and somatic stimulation evoked only a single somatic spike and did not trigger a dendritic Ca2+ plateau (Figure 3A, right).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: In the short morphology, Ca2+ plateaus could only be evoked by the largest coincident current injections (0.5 nA, ± 1 ms).
source: In the short morphology, Ca2+ plateaus could only be evoked by the largest coincident current injections (0.5 nA, ± 1 ms).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: The short neuron model never exhibited BAC firing even with increased Ca2+ conductance and the largest coincident dendritic injection.
source: While the dendritic voltage integral scaled similarly to the long morphology, showing active contribution of Ca2+ currents (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), the short neuron model never exhibited BAC firing.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Neither the length of the hot zone nor the HVA:LVA ratio had a substantial effect on the difference between long and short morphologies in dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis or BAC firing.
source: Neither the length of the hot zone (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,F) nor the HVA:LVA ratio (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D) had a substantial effect on the difference between long and short morphologies in dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis, BAC firing, or on somatic ADP measures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The presence of a Ca2+ plateau depended strongly on apical trunk length and was only sensitive to gCa above a critical length of approximately 350 µm (≅ 0.35 λ).
source: The presence of a Ca2+ plateau depended strongly on apical trunk length and was only sensitive to gCa above a critical length of approximately 350 µm (≅ 0.35 λ).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Below a critical length of approximately 350 µm, no Ca2+ plateaus were triggered regardless of how high gCa was set to.
source: Below this length, no Ca2+ plateaus were triggered regardless of how high gCa was set to.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: The width and peak voltage in the tuft increased steadily with dendritic length, even in the absence of Ca2+ conductances (gCa = 0).
source: Interestingly, the width and peak voltage in the tuft increased steadily with dendritic length (Figure 4B,C), even in the absence of Ca2+ conductances (gCa = 0).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4B,C.

claim: In the presence of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, the increased amplitude of bAPs triggered a large all-or-none Ca2+ plateau above a certain threshold length.
source: In the presence of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, the increased amplitude of bAPs triggered a large all-or-none Ca2+ plateau above a certain threshold length.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Removing Na+ channels caused a substantial reduction in peak voltage and width of the depolarization in the distal trunk, and abolished the trend of increasing tuft voltages with longer dendritic trunks.
source: Removing these channels caused a substantial reduction in peak voltage and width of the depolarization in the distal trunk, and importantly also abolished the trend of increasing tuft voltages with longer dendritic trunks (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4D,E.

claim: Active propagation caused bAPs to be larger and broader at all distances along a long dendrite compared to the same absolute distances in shorter dendrites.
source: More generally, active propagation caused bAPs to be larger and broader at all distances along a long dendrite compared to the same absolute distances in shorter dendrites (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: In a passive dendrite, voltage attenuation depends almost exclusively on distance and not trunk length.
source: This is not the case in a passive dendrite, where voltage attenuation depends almost exclusively on distance and not trunk length (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), bar the end-effect in the last segment.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: When all the various conductances were uniformly distributed along the apical trunk, the enhanced voltage continued to trigger Ca+ plateaus only in neurons with long apical trunks.
source: When all the various conductances were uniformly distributed along the apical trunk, the waveforms did not substantially change, and the enhanced voltage continued to trigger Ca+ plateaus only in neurons with long apical trunks (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tuft peak voltage remained positively correlated with apical trunk length even after the total removal of Ih.
source: Crucially, tuft peak voltage remained positively correlated with apical trunk length even after the total removal of Ih (i.e. had positive slope), contrary to changes observed with varying the amount of sodium current in the apical trunk (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis remained dependent on apical trunk length with varying Ih, albeit with the actual threshold length tracking the changes in Ih.
source: Furthermore, dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis remained dependent on apical trunk length, albeit with the actual threshold length tracking the changes in Ih (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Both width and voltage integral increased monotonically with trunk length regardless of the specific value of Ra in both the tuft and the last segment of the trunk.
source: However, in these simulations both width and voltage integral increased monotonically with trunk length regardless of the specific value of Ra in both the tuft and the last segment of the trunk.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Ra is not the primary determinant for generating the length-dependent effect on dendritic excitability.
source: This indicates that, although important, Ra is not the primary determinant for generating the length-dependent effect and if Ra indeed correlates with length, these effects may combine to further enhance the tuft voltage in long neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of computational modeling results.

claim: The temporal broadening of the depolarization can at least partially account for increased peak tuft voltage via a passive mechanism.
source: While it might seem counterintuitive that peak tuft voltage is increasing when trunk voltage is decreasing with length, we propose that the temporal broadening of the depolarization can at least partially account for this via a passive mechanism.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on computational modeling results.

claim: The tuft time constant and the width of the invading voltage pulse (e.g. bAP) interact to create a higher tuft depolarization with longer apical trunks.
source: These simulations show that the tuft time constant and the width of the invading voltage pulse (e.g. bAP) interact to create a higher tuft depolarization with longer apical trunks.
evidence: This is a conclusion from computational modeling experiments.

claim: There is a zone above a critical trunk integral for which many different width and depolarization combinations were sufficient to evoke a Ca2+ plateau in the tuft.
source: This revealed a zone above a critical trunk integral for which many different width and depolarization combinations were sufficient to evoke a Ca2+ plateau in the tuft (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: It is the complex interplay of width and amplitude with the tuft time constant that enables dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis.
source: These results show that it is the complex interplay of width and amplitude with the tuft time constant that enables dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Both BAC firing and cfADP were almost entirely absent in the V2m neurons.
source: We found that both BAC firing and cfADP were almost entirely absent in the V2m neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of primary experimental findings.

claim: The propensity for Ca2+ electrogenesis was positively correlated with the length of the apical dendrite trunk across all neurons.
source: Moreover, we observed that the propensity for Ca2+ electrogenesis was positively correlated with the length of the apical dendrite trunk across all neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of primary experimental findings.

claim: Both morphologically detailed and reduced models showed that decreasing the apical trunk length resulted in reduced propensity for dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis.
source: Both morphologically detailed and reduced models showed that decreasing the apical trunk length resulted in reduced propensity for dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary of computational modeling findings.

claim: The reduced propensity for dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis in short neurons is due to an interplay between bAP width, amplitude, and tuft impedance that depends critically on the presence of voltage-gated Na+ channels in the apical trunk.
source: Further simulations revealed that this is due to an interplay between bAP width, amplitude, and tuft impedance that depends critically on the presence of voltage-gated Na+ channels in the apical trunk.
evidence: This is a summary of computational modeling findings.

claim: The same cell type, in closely related and adjacent cortical areas, and under the same operating conditions can have a very different computational repertoire.
source: These results show that the same cell type, in closely related and adjacent cortical areas, and under the same operating conditions can have a very different computational repertoire.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental findings.

claim: The findings are inconsistent with the notion of canonical computations at the single cell level.
source: Our findings are thus inconsistent with the notion of canonical computations at the single cell level, suggesting they may not exist at the circuit level either.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental findings.

claim: Canonical computations may not exist at the circuit level.
source: Our findings are thus inconsistent with the notion of canonical computations at the single cell level, suggesting they may not exist at the circuit level either.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion extrapolated from the single-cell findings.

claim: Inhibition is one key factor known to control dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis.
source: One key factor known to control dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis is inhibition (Pérez-Garci et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: GABAB receptors were pharmacologically blocked to create more favourable conditions for BAC firing.
source: To determine the role of inhibition on the observed differences between V1 and V2m neurons, we pharmacologically blocked GABAB receptors, thus creating more favourable conditions for BAC firing.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The same experimental protocols and conditions were used across all experiments to make comparisons rigorous.
source: To make comparisons rigorous, we have used the same experimental protocols and conditions across all experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Recordings were made only from two well-defined groups, identified either by their projection target or genetic label, to exclude bias in selecting ttL5 neurons.
source: Furthermore, to exclude bias in selecting ttL5 neurons, we have recorded only from two well-defined groups, identified either by their projection target or genetic label.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: Similarly diminished propensity for bursting was found in both groups of V2m neurons (retrogradely labeled and Colgalt2-Cre).
source: We found similarly diminished propensity for bursting in both groups of V2m neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: The same results were found under different physiologically relevant Ca2+ concentrations in the extracellular solution.
source: We have found the same results under different physiologically relevant concentrations.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: Decreased propensity of V2m ttL5 neurons for dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis is a robust phenomenon.
source: Altogether, these results show that decreased propensity of V2m ttL5 neurons for dendritic Ca2+ electrogenesis is a robust phenomenon.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings under various conditions.

claim: Recent structural MRI data shows a thinner cortical mantle in more medial and posterior parts of the cortex.
source: This data is consistent with recent structural MRI data showing a thinner cortical mantle in more medial and posterior parts of the cortex (Fletcher and Williams, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The same biophysical model applied to a shorter morphology resulted in a loss of BAC firing, independently of Ca2+ channel density.
source: Using an existing, prominent biophysical model designed to reproduce ttL5 properties such as BAC firing, we found that the same model applied to a shorter morphology resulted in a loss of BAC firing, independently of Ca2+ channel density.
evidence: This is a summary of computational modeling findings.

claim: A sharp cut-off was found at a length of 0.35 λ (≅ 350 µm in model space), below which no BAC firing could be evoked in the reduced model.
source: We found a sharp cut-off at a length of 0.35 λ (≅ 350 µm in model space), below which no BAC firing could be evoked.
evidence: This is a summary of computational modeling findings.

claim: The reduced model is based on rat neurons and the apical trunk and oblique dendrites are pooled into the same compartment.
source: We note, however, that the reduced model is based on rat neurons and the apical trunk and oblique dendrites are pooled into the same compartment.
evidence: This is a description of the computational model used.

claim: The numerical values of model length do not translate directly into apical trunk lengths for real mouse neurons.
source: Therefore, the numerical values of model length do not translate directly into apical trunk lengths for real mouse neurons.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the computational model.

claim: Voltage-gated Na+ channels in the apical dendrite were identified as a key factor for reproducing the results through simulations.
source: Through our simulations, we identified voltage-gated Na+ channels in the apical dendrite as a key factor for reproducing our results.
evidence: This is a summary of computational modeling findings.

claim: Sodium channels control dendritic excitability by supporting active backpropagation, resulting in reduced attenuation over distance.
source: Sodium channels control dendritic excitability by supporting active backpropagation, resulting in reduced attenuation over distance.
evidence: This is a conclusion from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Combined with a broadening of the bAP proportionally to trunk length (due to capacitive filtering), active backpropagation caused longer neurons to have larger voltage integrals in the distal trunk, leading to greater charging of the tuft.
source: Combined with a broadening of the bAP proportionally to trunk length (due to capacitive filtering), this caused longer neurons to have larger voltage integrals in the distal trunk, leading to greater charging of the tuft.
evidence: This is a conclusion from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Above a minimal threshold for peak trunk voltage, the primary determinant of peak tuft voltage is the time-averaged voltage in the trunk.
source: We hypothesised that, above a minimal threshold for peak trunk voltage, the primary determinant of peak tuft voltage is the time-averaged voltage in the trunk.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on computational modeling results.

claim: The overall voltage integral was more important for triggering Ca2+ plateaus than the particular combination of depolarization width and amplitude.
source: Supporting this view, we found that the overall voltage integral was more important for triggering Ca2+ plateaus than the particular combination of depolarization width and amplitude.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: Variations in density and activation properties of other voltage-gated channels may also influence dendritic excitability.
source: Variations in density and activation properties of other voltage-gated channels may also influence dendritic excitability.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential mechanisms.

claim: In the presence of Na+ channels, the bAP in neurons with longer trunks was larger and broader at every distance from the soma.
source: It is interesting to note that, in the presence of Na+ channels, the bAP in neurons with longer trunks was larger and broader at every distance from the soma.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling experiments.

claim: The data predicts that bAP width and amplitude measured at the same absolute distance from the soma will be larger in neurons with longer apical trunks.
source: Our data thus predicts that bAP width and amplitude measured at the same absolute distance from the soma will be larger in neurons with longer apical trunks.
evidence: This is a prediction based on computational modeling results.

claim: The models used lacked NMDA channels.
source: It is worth noting that the models we used lacked NMDA channels.
evidence: This is a description of the computational models used.

claim: NMDA spikes can significantly increase the ability of distal tuft input to trigger Ca2+ plateaus at the bifurcation.
source: Experimental evidence shows that NMDA spikes can significantly increase the ability of distal tuft input to trigger Ca2+ plateaus at the bifurcation.
evidence: This statement is based on established experimental knowledge.

claim: When NMDA spikes are triggered directly at the hot zone, they have very little contribution to Ca2+ plateaus.
source: However, when NMDA spikes are triggered directly at the hot zone, they have very little contribution to Ca2+ plateaus (Larkum et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The cfADP protocol is independent of synaptically released glutamate.
source: In addition, the cfADP protocol is independent of synaptically released glutamate, and hence we expect the lack of NMDA channels in the models to have no significant effect on dendritic Ca2+ plateaus.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol and an inference about model validity.

claim: The human ttL5 neuron was recently shown to have greater compartmentalization and reduced excitability compared to rat neurons despite being substantially longer.
source: For example, the human ttL5 neuron was recently shown to have greater compartmentalization and reduced excitability compared to rat neurons despite being substantially longer (Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2018).

claim: Human ttL5 neurons had reduced ion channel densities, which may be consistent with the predictions of the current study.
